geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the mass around a courtyard to produce a clearer public threshold and a more program-appropriate ground figure.
Increase the carved public space enough to function as a legible communal void.
Open the court toward the verified access side to activate the frontage.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing dominant mass into a courtyard-bearing composition so the public void becomes the primary spatial figure rather than a side effect.
Keep the carved void large enough to read as usable public ground while preserving a compact building body.
Align the opening with the program-frame access side so the street threshold becomes legible.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact bar in some views, but the split-wing/puncture logic is only partially resolved and does not yet fully support the neighborhood-living brief. The mass is legible and not badly damaged, yet the public threshold is weak: the blue access edge is met by a mostly sealed ground response rather than a clearly active void, notch, or court. The silhouette is more segmented and stepped than sectional, so it lacks a convincing usable terrace or communal section. Because the form is coherent in several views but not across all views, and because the access/public-space relationship is underdeveloped, it fails the program-fit hard pass despite reasonable repair integrity.
